main_issue: Whether the housewarming should serve alcohol (A's pre-bought drinks) or be alcohol-free because D objects on Buddhist grounds.

A-B.evidence: B offers to split cost (18), proposes a separate drinks table (20), then a no-alcohol party with repayment (26); A resists on non-money grounds (19) and never accepts, so only partial agreement.

A-C.evidence: C suggested a cooler (13) and backed the side table (21), then offered to repay A for a no-alcohol party (27); A never accepts and wants alcohol for guests.

A-D.evidence: A questions D's late objection (9, 15) and asks 'We can't have any alcohol at all?' (23); D says 'For me, yes' (24). Neither shifts.

B-C.evidence: C agrees with B's soft drinks (3, 5), calls the side table a good compromise (21), then backs the no-alcohol plan: 'I'll chip in' (27).

B-D.evidence: B's side-table compromise was rejected by D (22), then B proposes a no-alcohol party (26), which meets D's demand.

C-D.evidence: C's cooler idea was rejected by D (14), then C backs the no-alcohol party at 27, which meets D's position.
